We’re thrilled to announce the launch of our Delegators Reward Program, an opportunity for you to support the WorldMapPin project while earning rewards simultaneously. This is another big step in the evolution of this great project that we all love. ### How It All Started The idea popped out during a delightful breakfast at Hivefest when @roelandp asked @detlev and @lizanomadsoul if we had a plan about rewarding our delegators. Since then, we've put a lot of thought into creating a program that not only rewards you, our amazing supporters but also strengthens the Hive ecosystem. Big thank you to @arcange for coding and testing the system for the project. ### Why a Delegators Reward Program? The program aims at rewarding anyone who delegates at least 50 HP to @worldmappin in order to give back as a thank-you for their delegation. By delegating Hive Power to @worldmappin, you become an integral part of our project, supporting the curation of daily travel content and receiving a share of the curation rewards proportional to your delegation. The @worldmappin team curates travel content daily and votes for the best English and Spanish posts. Our curation rewards are quite high as we are very active in curating quality content. Our average curation APR ranges from 9% to 11%, which our delegators will also benefit from. ### How does it work? Several other projects on HIVE reward their delegators with HIVE, HBD, or with their own tokens. At @worldmappin, we have decided to reward our delegators with Hive Power (HP). The main reasons to do so are: - We will grow together - If you were doing your own curation, you would also receive Hive Power - It is a healthy way to support the Hive Eco System. We will share 80% of our curation rewards with our delegator. The remaining will be used to grow the @worldmappin account and provide greater rewards to the talented authors we curate. *Note: for efficiency reasons, we will not distribute a reward if its amount is less than 0.005 HP. With a delegation of at least 50 HP, this should not be an issue.* ### When? Our Delegators Reward Program will start on **November 1st**! This means we will collect data on curation rewards and delegations once the day is over. Only after that our delegators will receive their rewards. [Léelo en **español** aquí](#spanish)
![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/EphwvnseGpoFsqerip5DYGfvbjMnpcP2dKvEaiP5Ezhaad1uqpdt9YswSrDWH917stk.jpg) # Our goal at Worldmappin Map and Travel Community Since **the worldmappin.com map** exists we have planned to extend it for all Hive users, which means everyone can pin their post on the map and link it to the content-related community - bringing all the users and communities together in one place again the worldmappin.com map. **The Worldmappin Community** is the start of showing how that works. It always has been and will be travel-related, because our vision in this **community** has always been two things: A: Provide each traveler with their unique world map, where they can explore the world, pin their trips and memories, and dive back into the memories whenever they want with just a click. B: Give the travelers a platform to share their adventures and experiences with others, so that the whole community benefits from using the map as a travel guide to finding more information and inspiration for their next trips. As you know the curation team of @worldmappin project: @lizanomadsoul, @ybanezkim26, @lauramica, @glecerioberto, and @ninaeatshere, is checking the incoming travel posts of this community every day, curating the top content and giving the winners visibility in our Daily Travel Digest. We often get questions from our community members on what to do and not do, or how they can improve their content to get curated by our team. So we took some time within the team to write down our guidelines with all the rules and suggestions, on which you can rely when writing a travel post within the @Worldmappin community. In this post, we will go into detail about every one of them. - Thanks also to @livinguktaiwan and the rest of the @worldmappin team @detlev, @arcange, @godfish,@louis88, @rivalzzz, @masterswatch and @uniforced for your input and for the support on this. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 19.17.17.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23w3EVhVkZqLVzF3s3wB8HBA6aoHDSZnwZ4rjrPDKzQj9Gi5wqtBKyYnjq4EQXm7J79wT.png) For us, it is important, that all of you have the same knowledge and possibilities to position your content within this community following the standards of quality that we seek to ensure following our vision. ![Authorized picture by @bil.prag](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23tvkkLbUnByuUE82pY5LHSVDy7hfUmnA9fEPDvhmPzSGJBpQPekoqp9yUjqtax4CrvFY.jpeg) # Intro We love and celebrate the huge diversity in our community, representing different cultures, customs, mentalities, genders, age groups, and languages. Every traveler has his/her unique character, perception of the world, values, and strengths that make him/her the special person that we love to follow on their trips. We are very aware that with this uniqueness there comes different styles of writing, taking pictures or telling a story and that is super great! So of course, this summary is meant only as a suggestion! We love and understand that HIVE is a decentralized ecosystem, where we are all free to create content in our own individual way! However, if you share our goal and want to get support for your efforts, you may want to consider certain rules and suggestions for your future posts, that allow us to establish a standard of quality. # So let's get started! Read further and get more clear on these things on the way! ![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23xoueMQMECcMBErfM1aCGiDLJkg2Y2xcvtwnRnCg7WA5SBVSsTeKdAvV1teUt7yv6q75.jpg) ## Rules for posting in the community As you may know, every community has its own rules. The rules are our most important guidelines to follow our vision and keep the quality for every one of you. If you want to be in this community you have to follow them, otherwise you will be muted at some point. Those rules have been implemented since the beginning of the project and are regularly updated. ### Rule Nr. 1. This community is only for posts included in the https://worldmappin.com map. The most important rule of our community is to pin your post to our map, because for us it's not only important that you can collect your posts on your map, but also that other travelers can benefit from your experiences. Of course, this will also give your post more exposure, as well as a chance to be featured in our daily Travel Digest 😃. There are two ways to pin your post to the map: - Include PINs from PeakD: After writing your post, click on the map icon at the bottom. It's next to “ Short preview description” and above the “Advanced” icon. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 20.00.51.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/Eo6SchkLfuZGRfoyFcwgv3N2WiVnFNP38U8cifkis662bFNF1j2PzpwdcYQDjD7Amhq.png) - Include PINs in the rest of the Front-ends: - Go to https://worldmappin.com/ - Find the location of your publication on the map, you can do this by scrolling the map or using the search bar. - Click on the GET CODE button and then click on the exact location of your publication: a code snippet will be generated. - Copy the code and paste it into the draft of your Hive post. Then publish it. 🙂 - The code will be invisible in your post, but a few minutes after publishing you will receive a comment informing you that your post has been added to the map. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 20.01.24.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23wgUJT7kkrRyKQsXSLrRbivrgJ18h3sPeyGJVnZFTJDV8H1Xco8EN1zcJdXtpDQrCQUo.png) ### Rule Nr. 2. English and Spanish content only. (or bi-lingual with one of the languages being English or Spanish) As we want this map to be understandable for most of our users and we are still growing. We only allow English or Spanish content for now. Of course we plan to extend this rule to more languages over time but for now only those two languages are allowed and being curated. If your native language is not English, feel free to include the original version of your writing in your native language next to the English or Spanish text. ### Rule Nr. 3. Only original content, no plagiarism, no AI-generated content, no recycled content. We want to know what you experienced! See your Pictures and get shared your personal knowledge - so we can be on the trip together and follow your adventures just the way you did! So please only use information, pictures, or videos that are yours (or put the source). Plagiarism is not allowed because of obvious reasons. We know that AI is the future, it is fun and that of course it can help put more value on your post sometimes, but there are also some users out there, who are writing their posts using AI only - trying to use it only to get some payout - not to share their trip experiences with others. So for us, a mix is ok, but we will know if it is 100% AI generated and that is fully against our rules as it is also not you - and therefore not following our vision and values. Recycling old posts and pictures same as writing multiple times about the same place /the same experience is not allowed for the same reasons. ### Rule Nr. 4. Content must be about places you have personally traveled to and about your experience. We want you to explore your own map, make your own experiences and share them with the community, so they get inspired to do something like that as well! We love to be on your side when you are getting out of your comfort zone, taking on new adventures and checking out new places. So don´t just plan it theoretically - go, do it, and write about it after you experience it yourself! ### Rule Nr. 5. Worldmappin is a travel community, please post reviews of accommodations, food, and restaurants in other appropriate communities. Please avoid posting on unrelated topics. This also includes - reviews about accommodations - shopping malls - restaurants - tips & tricks on transportation unless they are only a small part of your trip and not the main topic of the post OR such a place of interest to travel to, because of historic /extra cool background. However, you can pin your posts from other communities on the map, to keep track of all your visits on https://worldmappin.com. Here are some examples (click on each image to see details): |[Actifit community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-193552/created) |[BEER community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-187719/created) |[HiveFest community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-106258/created)| |-|-|-| |
[![](https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://usermedia.actifit.io/D9DCB68D-D042-45C3-80E3-739DF4AE1581638640735517426688)](https://peakd.com/hive-193552/@ninaeatshere/actifit-ninaeatshere-20241009t182346898z)
|
[![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbpc9YajQkcxGv9kMtTkGGXMLfq3B4WSTKiriGbKDXBXz/img_3344.jpg)](https://peakd.com/hive-187719/@ninaeatshere/beer-tasting-at-hivefest-split)
| [![](https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EoGyotE2GeJxou8KqraF6yzEnaPDAYshQ2Q4njiwdHRzCKxJCNQdauwGysDMKm9XWzx.jpeg)](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@ninaeatshere/restaurant-gusar-hivefest-gala-dinner-or-engesp) | | [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Eo2BSgYeWqHyJeFCtZdKFTZdQcDyUJUersW5YPavQEspAyECJkZbG9sjAc6m2noLD6i.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-193552/@worldmappin/wmp1728499187646)| [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tHbkj8CLsRWaYya87AmM3xbgqg1UYTcLfvycps5qRkU18MhVUwRfMvGWquhuWrVmesi.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-187719/@worldmappin/wmp1727017768292)| [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tHbg1MP4BtYk2Qt8dEtzJ46Ld83kwSwpzMEZVNeGrJD9ojyvgMQpVyPsqFFjQJ9HmH6.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@worldmappin/wmp1726526214980)| ### Rule Nr. 6. Penalties that happen if you don´t follow the rules If you don´t follow our community rules, you will be muted. Depending on which rule you are breaking, you get a warning and will be watched or muted right away. As the general consensus within Hive is that plagiarized content, AI-generated, spam, and recycled posts meant to farm rewards are to be muted, and users involved in those activities are to be penalized by blacklisting from further curation, here we are very strict and act right away. If you break one of the other rules you will get a friendly reminder and will be put on our watchlist. If it happens again you will be muted again. - If you are having trouble with this or you have questions on it you can get in touch with us on [Discord Channel](https://discord.gg/EGtBvSM) at any time. ![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/EqBbJbYvcJYiErfDBaRHrRiwc7M95b4LRZV3u1CUZwZRuQR1MDpFsiiZEcvbCSTrTqv.jpeg) ## Suggestions Congrats! You have made it through the rule jungle and are enjoying the view as all the fog should be gone by now. As a big thank you for your attention and because you are a great member of this community, we want to give you a small collection of suggestions to make your content even more exciting for others to read. Of course, those things can also help to be selected by us in the daily Traveldigest. ### Headline of the post On Hive, hundreds of posts are published every day, so it is very difficult for curators to cover all the content. The title we choose is the first piece of information we see from your work, so it is important that the title of your post is short, attractive, and related to the content you submit. There is no single way, but in terms of travel content, it is advisable to indicate the location or the name of the place you visit instead or in addition to your invitation to read the content of an adventure. It is recommended to avoid long titles, there is just no need to detail itineraries or exalt the headline, so get to the point 😎. ### Bilingual posts As we told you already in the rules section: If your native language is not English, feel free to include the original version of your writing in your native language. This helps us to verify the authenticity of the text and allows you to have a wider audience and interactions with people who also speak the same language as you. Of course, always include the English translation. When you do so, please make it visually attractive and easy to follow. As for the way to distribute the content in different languages, there are many possibilities (one language first followed by the other, translation by blocks of content or in different columns, among others) and all of them are valid, the important thing is that the way you present it allows the reader to feel comfortable when reading your content. Try to put yourself on the reader's side. As for the **title**, try to point out the languages in which it is available, no need to be redundant. Here are some examples, there can be many variations of this, but the best is to indicate only once in the sentence the presence of each language: *e.g.1 “My post headline [Eng][Esp]” e.g.2 “El título de mi post [Esp][Eng]” e.g.3 “My post headline | El título de mi post”*. ### Length of content Travel and adventure are words that by themselves open our imagination to countless stories. Remember that our goal in this community is to invite others to accompany us during the travels and serve as a guide to visit. You write about your experiences and let others know about the spots you have enjoyed the most. It is difficult to summarize them in just 300 words. Of course you can, but is it enough to make your experience the best of the day? By this, we don't mean that we write a lot just to increase volume, nor that your publications have to be full of historical/technical data obtained from other sources. What we love is for you to take us on a journey with you, with your emotions and sensations through the journey that many can make, but that has been unique for you. The moment you to tell us your own story, what particularly inspired you to talk about it, it is not difficult to reach **at least 500 words**, which could be considered as a starting point to stand out. ![Authorized gif by @ninaeatshere](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xVMRr2moLd8z8im7sHAq2k8EfG9PfHVPrcL9fZG5vGYtn18KNTspFHUgTZai8xPZed6.gif) ### Photos and videos This is another important feature that immediately captures the reader's attention. Choosing and highlighting your images can be crucial when promoting your publication, but you must not forget that the essence of a travel post is your story, the experience, and the anecdotes that allow you to capture those moments with which you illustrate your blog. We recommend finding a balance between photos and text. You can use as many photos as you want, but remember that these serve as backup to your story, this community is not about photography, so publishing 20 photos and 100 words, is not as interesting as a travel guide. On the other side sharing only 3 images that do not highlight that incredible journey is also not telling so much about your adventure. Therefore, a basic recommendation would be to include at least 5 photos of the environment we visited, showing the landscape, the town, or the monuments. Taking pictures of ourselves during the tour, selfies, and photos of food and lodging is super nice to see, but cannot be the main part of the audiovisual material, remember that the community is focused on the traveler's destination. Try to take care of the quality of the photographs. Lack of focus and leaning without seeking dynamism or any other form of artistic expression, end up in images that are difficult to understand. As for **the videos, regardless of the length, there is no justifying the lack of text and images** sharing our experience. Not everyone has the time to watch a whole video, the best thing is to offer the viewer both options so that we not only have video views but also invite readers to enjoy our experience. We recommend orienting the device used for recording horizontally so that it is more friendly to the eye in 3Speak. ### Sources, quotations, rights, and credits We have emphasized the importance of sharing original content, based on personal experience and according to rules 3 and 4 of the community, so it might go without saying that the text, images, and other resources used in the publication must be our own. However, for specific occasions within the post, when we share an image or video **authorized** by third parties, we must give credit to the authors and link to the source link to verify its veracity. This is not a problem if we do not base our entire article on someone else's reference, but we introduce an element to improve the story we have been sharing with others. ### Tags In any case, in Hive tags must be related to the content you are writing about. Within the community, we don't require any in particular, but #Travel will help you classify your content, making it more accessible when someone is interested in this topic. Some relevant monuments or features of the place visited are #beach, #nature, #forest, #mountain, #lake. If you include a language other than English, use the tag of your language of origin and some reference to travel (e.g. #Spanish, #viajes, #senderismo #deutsch). ![Authorized picture by @louis88](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpvhuUYiyc9pAWJeemu1ss6qhkNptprFMgLr5LDuNr4KGWC9YLjkQxZGjS57ReLovws.jpeg) # Engagement Last but not least, as important as all the previous sections, the commitment of each user within the blockchain and especially in the community is fundamental. Has conseguido atravesar la jungla de reglas y estás disfrutando de la vista, ya que toda la niebla debería haberse disipado ya. Como gran agradecimiento por tu atención y porque eres un gran miembro de esta comunidad, queremos darte una pequeña colección de sugerencias para que tu contenido sea aún más emocionante de leer para los demás. Por supuesto, esas cosas también pueden ayudar a ser seleccionado por nosotros en el Traveldigest diario. ### Título del post En Hive se publican cientos de posts cada día, por lo que es muy difícil para los curadores abarcar todo el contenido. El título que elegimos es la primera información que vemos de tu trabajo, por lo que es importante que el título de tu publicación sea corto, atractivo y esté relacionado con el contenido que presentas. No hay una forma única, pero en términos de contenido de viaje, es aconsejable indicar la ubicación o el nombre del lugar que visitas en vez, o además, de tu invitación a leer el contenido de una aventura. Se recomienda evitar los títulos largos, no hace falta detallar itinerarios ni exaltar el título, así que ve al grano 😎. ### Publicaciones bilingües Como ya te dijimos en la sección de normas: Si tu lengua materna no es el inglés, no dudes en incluir la versión original de tu escrito en tu lengua de origen. Esto nos ayuda a verificar la autenticidad del texto y te permite tener una audiencia más amplia e interactuar con personas que también hablan el mismo idioma que tú. Por supuesto, incluye siempre la traducción al inglés. Cuando lo hagas, procura que sea visualmente atractivo y fácil de seguir. En cuanto a la forma de distribuir el contenido en diferentes idiomas, hay muchas posibilidades (un idioma primero seguido del otro, traducción por bloques de contenido o en diferentes columnas, entre otras) y todas son válidas, lo importante es que la forma en que lo presentes permita al lector sentirse cómodo al momento de leer tu contenido. Intenta ponerte en el lugar del lector. En cuanto al **título**, intenta señalar los idiomas en los que está disponible, no hace falta ser redundante. He aquí algunos ejemplos, puede haber muchas variantes, pero lo mejor es indicar una sola vez en la frase la presencia de cada idioma: *e. j.1 "El título de mi post [Esp][Eng]" e. j. 2 "My post headline [Eng][Esp]" e. j. 3 "El título de mi post | My post headline"*. ### Extensión del contenido Viaje y aventura son palabras que por sí solas despiertan nuestra imaginación a innumerables historias. Recuerda que nuestro objetivo en esta comunidad es invitar a otros a acompañarnos durante los viajes y servir de guía para su visita. Escribe sobre tus experiencias y da a conocer a los demás los lugares que más te han gustado. Es difícil resumirlos en sólo 300 palabras. Claro que puedes, pero ¿es suficiente para que tu experiencia sea la mejor de todas a lo largo del día? Con esto no queremos decir que escribas mucho sólo para incrementar el volumen, ni que tus publicaciones tengan que estar llenas de datos históricos/técnicos obtenidos de otras fuentes. Lo que nos encanta es que nos lleves de viaje contigo, con tus emociones y sensaciones a través del recorrido que muchos pueden hacer, pero que para ti ha sido único. En el momento en que nos cuentes tu propia historia, lo que te ha inspirado especialmente para hablar de ello, no es difícil llegar a **al menos 500 palabras**, lo que podría considerarse como un punto de partida para sobresalir. ![Gif autorizado por @ninaeatshere](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/241tQTPAaoSvjN9G5z3mBNQS3XaSMPsPBceZbR5WwdZXYC9pHGsm2VAdJwwrLX1icFiib.gif) ### Fotos y vídeos Este es otro elemento importante que capta inmediatamente la atención del lector. Elegir y destacar tus imágenes puede ser crucial a la hora de promocionar tu publicación, pero no debes olvidar que la esencia de un post de viajes es tu historia, la experiencia y las anécdotas que te permiten capturar esos momentos con los que ilustras tu blog. Te recomendamos que encuentres un equilibrio entre fotos y texto. Puedes utilizar todas las fotos que quieras, pero recuerda que éstas sirven de respaldo a tu historia, esta comunidad no es de fotografía, por lo que publicar 20 fotos y 100 palabras, no es tan interesante para una guía de viajes. Por otro lado compartir solo 3 imágenes que no resalten aquel increíble viaje tampoco está contando mucho sobre tu aventura. Por lo tanto, una recomendación básica sería incluir al menos 5 fotos del entorno que visitamos, mostrando el paisaje, el pueblo, o los monuments. Hacernos fotos durante el recorrido, selfies, fotos de la comida y el alojamiento es súper agradable de ver, pero no puede ser la parte principal del material audiovisual, recuerda que la comunidad se centra en el destino del viajero. Trata de cuidar la calidad de las fotografías. La falta de enfoque y el inclinarlas, sin buscar dinamismo o cualquier otra forma de expresión artística, acaban en imágenes difíciles de entender. En cuanto a **los vídeos, independientemente de su duración, no se justifica la falta de texto e imágenes** compartiendo nuestra experiencia. No todo el mundo tiene tiempo de ver un vídeo entero, lo mejor es ofrecer al espectador las dos opciones, para que no sólo tengamos visualizaciones del vídeo, sino que invitemos a los lectores a disfrutar de nuestra experiencia. Te recomendamos orientar el dispositivo utilizado para la grabación en horizontal, para que sea más amigable a la vista en 3Speak. ### Fuentes, citas, derechos y créditos Hemos hecho hincapié en la importancia de compartir contenido original, basado en la experiencia personal y de acuerdo con las reglas 3 y 4 de la comunidad, por lo que puede que no haga falta decir que el texto, las imágenes y otros recursos utilizados en la publicación deben ser propios. Sin embargo, en ocasiones puntuales dentro del post, cuando compartamos una imagen o vídeo **autorizado** por terceros, deberemos dar crédito a los autores y enlazar al link de la fuente para comprobar su veracidad. Esto no es un problema si no basamos todo nuestro artículo en la referencia de otra persona, sino que introducimos un elemento para mejorar la historia que hemos compartido con los demás. ### Etiquetas En todo momento, las etiquetas en Hive deben estar relacionadas con el contenido sobre el que escribes. Dentro de la comunidad, no exigimos ninguna en particular, pero #Travel te ayudará a clasificar tu contenido, haciéndolo más accesible cuando alguien se interese por este tema. Lo mismo ocurre cuando incluyes en las etiquetas la ciudad, el país o la región que estás visitando. También puedes utilizar referencias a la forma de viajar, #backpacking, #roadtrip, #solotravel, #hiking, entre otras. Algunos monumentos o características relevantes del lugar visitado son #beach, #nature, #forest, #mountain, #lake. Sólo para facilitar la búsqueda de contenidos similares, en caso de que alguien se interese por el artículo debido a esa mención concreta. En definitiva, aquí buscamos compartir nuestra pasión por viajar: #wanderlust. Si incluyes un idioma que no sea el inglés, utiliza la etiqueta de tu idioma de origen y alguna referencia a los viajes (por ejemplo, #spanish, #viajes, #senderismo #deutsch). ![Foto autorizada por @louis88](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpvhuUYiyc9pAWJeemu1ss6qhkNptprFMgLr5LDuNr4KGWC9YLjkQxZGjS57ReLovws.jpeg) # Compromiso Por último, tan importante como todos los apartados anteriores, es fundamental el compromiso de cada usuario dentro de la blockchain y especialmente en la comunidad. Si esperamos recibir apoyo, lo más razonable es apoyar a los creadores de contenido que hacen el mismo esfuerzo que nosotros y que dan vida a nuestro universo viajero. Ser un miembro activo de una comunidad no significa sólo publicar en ella, sino interactuar con otros usuarios en las publicaciones de la comunidad más allá de responder a los comentarios de nuestros posts. Votar, comentar y aportar opiniones son formas de apoyarnos mutuamente, compartir experiencias, ponernos en contacto, hacer nuevas amistades y, por supuesto, aprender y añadir valor real al ecosistema. *One of my favorite views, overlooking the taro fields near Hanalei town.*

  Of all the Hawaiian islands, where tourism is allowed, I have been to the island of Kauai the least. Now I find myself sent her for research and development, a bit of scouting, for a new addition to our Hawaii UnCruise expedition offering. We are looking into the possibility of adding a four night land package that guests could sign up for, before joining the expedition ship. So I didn't waste any time in getting a private local driver to guide us all over the islands hot spots, and lesser known spots as well.

   After an early morning exploratory walk through the tourist hub of Poipu, Dan and I drove to the Kauai Inn, near Nauwiliwili Harbor, where we would meet our guide for the day. Gray, our guide/driver, was waiting for us when we pulled in. We jumped into the black SUV and set out to explore. We kept Gray talking for the next six hours as he showed us the can't miss waterfalls, temples, beaches, and views, while also pointing out some of the behind the scenes local favorites. We even stopped in Kailua at a bakery/coffee/pizza place....which just about combines all my favorite things. 

   One of my favorite hidden gems was running across some nesting Laysan albatross down this neighborhood culdesac. We might see these once or twice a season in the southern islands, but here they were, just chilling in the round-a-bout with a big, fluffy baby. The overlooks were gorgeous. It reminded me that this island can really be seen and enjoyed by just about anyone. You don't need a high level of fitness to see amazing sights, right from your car. However, if you can head onto some trails or explore beaches, then the island really opens up. 

   Kauai's claim to fame is that it was the only island never conquered by Kamehameha. It has been hit hard by hurricanes in recent times, but the rains soak in quickly. It does have the worlds wettest place near the top of the volcano. Waimea Canyon is another unique feature, sometimes being called the Grand Canyon of the Pacific. The island feels lush, as you can see by all the shades of green in the picture above. Its worth a visit...and when you do, look up Gray, he'll show you all the places.

*A rare Hawaiian monk seal swims near the beach. I saw this one playing with another, just offshore, early in the morning. Kauai is one of the best places to get views of these endangered animals.*

![IMG_5459.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EqquPbiRLVvg6GGwPPJMG3VqzCKyS8LUFquQsyDATehFZnWCFR6Q3PaBGZQARj7PXie.jpeg)

*Another stop on our circle island tour: Tunnels Beach.
*
![IMG_5512.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EqNFEp2FJU2A44HK33mQeUyC6x9eaoyZdgbc53auLeZiMLZuwrvDytVfn115SCDriNi.jpeg)

*A large green sea turtle rest on the shores of Poipu.*

*This was an old church in Hanalei town that I happened to catch during a photo shoot.*

*I had to get a photo of me next to this giant sisal plant. These plants are known for their stiff fibers, which can be made into rope.*

Normally, I don't go on hikes in November either, but as I miss exploring the outdoors, I was determined to head to Mount Bismo in Dieng, Wonosobo. Last week, a friend and I set off from Pekalongan on a motorcycle. The distance we had to travel was about 90 km or three hours of estimated travel. Because the journey we were about to take was relatively long and the terrain was not easy, my friend and I decided to leave early in the morning. At around 5:30am, we departed from Kajen sub-district. The road was still deserted at that time, so it was easy for us to speed up to get there quickly.
.
It was almost 09.00 am when we entered Wonosobo Regency. We both decided to have breakfast first. Apart from the fact that we hadn't eaten anything since we left home, we also ate to recharge our energy before the hike. After breakfast, my friend and I rushed to Sikunang Village where the climbing base camp that we would use. Registration or SIMAKSI (permit to enter the conservation area) is Rp 30,000/person.
--- ![IMG20231120084650.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/Eos2D65YmJWi6go8LoErtMxEN5fnb63UZG6truTgnfjb8RfZmKGRs5df7mi83VpPWGC.jpg) ![IMG20231120084848.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/EoAan8nR3DW9MUajn7GfpiuPYCdphjvPEaWFzXsXaQZ7iw7VyAnWBtUjZaqnUthSEXH.jpg) ![IMG20231120085412.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23x1BdmhGxJoiqsYRHvGQjjqPWW5kPtmsYhjb2hgegmckDHfMZqmfF5b2TsPHDfAQXLnT.jpg) --- .
As an additional story, this was also my first time climbing without camping. My friend and I wanted to walk leisurely to the top, then rest for a while and go down again. So, we didn't bring a carrier bag and only packed enough food and drinks to consume during the hike break. After completing the simaksi, tidying up the necessities, finally we set out!
_____
***POS 1-2***
_____
The journey from the basecamp to post 1 is a path that is still in the area of residents' fields. So along the way to post two, the left and right are potato fields. After about thirty minutes of travel, the path began to thicken. This is a sign that we have almost reached post 2. My friend and I have not felt tired at all. We kept walking, until soon we reached post 2. We took a short break and took photos right in front of the gate.
--- ![IMG20231120133035.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/243qFT8LHDuFLijT6RqC7dLrkZomP25SkS87ehYxSJYj1MirDPJL8HCrd2qQk8bqh3dQW.jpg) ![IMG20231120131919.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23uFRuwLwA5QwbBoWBhMpmmJf3bCw2D1T6w36yHu5Nd6fu5Lq62LWCgy6h2z86yGhSxnp.jpg) ![IMG20231120125306.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/243WZs2KkU2UgMtFe89iNaFjWX6CnLbCEVr4X7vuVjPdsvHTznvhCps2qMgLZ8DimdWMV.jpg) ![IMG20231120130131.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23uFS1hwpJPypvTJkDuALWYD3xQCRwwMFq3M1NWc4euLeCsxZh1Mky5TZ8r9AbFnFBCSU.jpg) --- .
From the gate the track has started to enter the forest and it looks like the fog is starting to descend. I had a hunch that it would be fog all day. The path along post 2 is in the form of dirt steps and roots. Since it wasn't raining, it wasn't slippery. But it was clear that the ground was damp. The steps make it easy for hikers to step on. It doesn't take long to reach post three, it only takes fifteen minutes. There is a large signpost that marks that it has arrived at post 3, the path has started to climb slightly with the terrain still remaining the same in the form of soil and roots. Not far from the post 3 marker, there was a closed stall. My friend and I sat there for a while because the scenery in the town of Dieng below looked beautiful.
_____
***POST 3-CAMP AREA***
_____
The forest is not too dense here and is a heterogeneous forest. After a short hike from post 3 I found that the trail began to open up and slope. Fun fact: during my hikes to several mountains, this is the mountain with the best slope! I can even run in this area. A few meters later, I entered cam area1. On this route via Sikunang, the camp area is divided into two. Here and another one above near the highest peak, Puncak Indraprasta. Camp area 1 is not spacious, but elongated, usually climbers prefer to build a post in camp area 2, because it is more spacious. ---- ![IMG20231120100112.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/245mrQyDackKzUiVn9qGsZNxVm66jipdE2sZC1dqRmny1ahGH2pBYiYj384t6FozK4dny.jpg) ![IMG20231120094831.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23xVGe7fqaCKv6AQeuzCMNZA6C1FB8zEtQF4Pg5nvRiAUHDxUDkpsu84YrM8vEebKVxXq.jpg) ![IMG20231120095411.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23xemxhe36eoj8drn227qtgWtvuwo4JpdSAmMvgM74MHWLCieA8yY7nN5D9TLT6w4ymri.jpg) ![IMG20231120100238.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23ujk8pUrHSRSFi4cZZkEc2f4ANTk9yzZAutHMN4Gz4WYVsCv6ToqDkoiDHwF5dosii6C.jpg) ![IMG20231120095053.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23xKvhrKgTQX8QcpJFgJcLovvjLReqWvp5k7hqQfPSbT1A11vDfXhJv2d8drWhQM4jAXf.jpg) ![IMG20231120100117.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23xKvd5UuxTkHcDGH1DRM6Lw7hu3ywmDwkzQ7wiqzSkNXzjYLbGjdwQGKYEAtoYnR2Wfj.jpg) --- Here, many fern trees begin to grow. Both small and large. After exhausting the camp area, we reached the first peak of Sikunang, Puncak Tugel at 2332 meters above sea level.
.
Everything was covered in fog! ---- ![IMG20231120110026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/246azcGiYn4z7vdBwJd8h5CGYiVxQL5EWeyves89R1Z9gkq24VvnP3dFoRyabq19kjhoR.jpg) ![IMG20231120105629.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/EnWJwVFuEEeAxtvZYUHeteNEFBwQxc2XwkiyTEGF6mwKiDKnTJFsoVu2yM8Qz9g58nt.jpg) ![IMG20231120102244.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/246b2m5hs7zm2ho2cCyDhR52Xksn4WCuf61zX3UbSHUUPJffcYGfaXew1CZzk5qZHrBZJ.jpg) Hello everyone! --- If it's sunny, the view here is very beautiful. However, Dieng is often foggy these days according to the officer at the registration site. My friend and I sat down to rest while enjoying our supplies. We had a nice chat because we weren't in a hurry. After re-energizing, we continued our journey.
_____ _____
***PEAK NEMU-NEMU AND PEAK INDRAPRASTA***
----- ![IMG_0296.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23zkkZUmDUZHnEAJJFL5Et4RMzWx6sDupvab2wpd4pnp1YCn2RBoLLL3z18dsQuk8B9jq.JPG) ![IMG20231120110611.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23vYjNxuDmnRoP2DbKmkTCXsTtwPANDFBQbndu71fdYm1RF1etrycsjSBiHnGM52mGoPD.jpg) ![IMG20231120102334.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/23v4bmGK9daEFhTT4DqXcUtJFbP2PHBttatdu4EWzPmRbbgBpY5CGt3Ypge6pzHUW5wm7.jpg) ![IMG20231120110258.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/titisnariyah/246GFWhhAHLPPVgQoHh1FnWPGWQ2DSU1iWH4EHvqYFXmDhYMXsdTbjjNruACnbwuyxhC4.jpg) ---
The next path is narrower as it is a ridge. It will continue like this until the summit. By the way, Mount Bismo has at least five peaks. Three peaks are obtained through the Sikunang trail, while the other two peaks are through the Silandak trail. As I said before, I will only get to the highest peak. So, the other two peaks, I did not visit.
.
Fifteen minutes after Tugel Peak, there is a second peak, Nemu-Nemu Peak at 2348 meters above sea level. Although the sun was already visible, the fog was still low. I was a little hopeful that by the time I reached Indraprasta, the lengit would open up and I could get a beautifuloke. view. Ridge after ridge was passed, the path began to narrow. Along the way, we did not meet any other hikers. I did this hike on a Monday, so there weren't many hikers.
.
Not too long ago, we finally reached the second camp area. This is a very large arena and is located jutting inward. Not right on the hiking trail. This area can be used to set up dozens of tents. For hiking groups, I highly recommend this cam on the Sikunang trail. There is a sign that says you are allowed to camp up to the camp boundary. Not long from this area, the highest peak of Mount Bisma was visible. Here we go, the highest peak of Indraprasta at 2365 meters above sea level.Yeah... finally. Although it was foggy, slowly the blue clouds came into view. My friend and I relaxed for a while, enjoyed the clean air, and finished our lunch (except for drinks, because we still had to leave drinks for the descent). After almost thirty minutes, we finally decide to go home. Looks like I'll have to come back here during the sunny days. I wanted to show you guys, the view would have been so pretty if there was no fog. But, it's okay, I'm not too disappointed, I'm just happy to finally sniff the mountain air...

## Good night to all my beloved hive friends ♥️ ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUnKNEqsBYdEPtjPETrXQfkNKmzb6ChArTnfQnYR317V6/1775725362490.jpg) In this post I will share my experience while exploring the route on the edge of the tawar sea and the discovery of several popular tourist destinations,in this post we will see several areas that have been damaged by floods several months ago in Aceh, related to Aceh Tengah being in the highland area so the floods here are not too bad but experienced a fairly severe landslide, many areas have been damaged, some tourist destinations have even disappeared, but this all happened due to natural factors that were completely unexpected. Every incident will definitely leave an unforgettable impression and memory, whether it is good or bad also depends on how we go through it, look at some of the pictures below. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSJjxh62KrFA4esqqhXaJniJqR1j69Pj11CneZ7StctUQ/1775725362737.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaUNSsAbf3Gio6owE6PkmjZeRoEDpfFnrAWKbmQnBdDUh/1775725362816.jpg) This is a natural view around Mandale village, this village is located at the foot of the mountains and is also quite close to the tawar sea, here we can see many mountainous areas that have experienced landslides, some of which have even damaged many public facilities and buried roads, I can't imagine how horrific the scene was when the landslide occurred. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUTiy6borXvLmt2rqrMsEXJ5xD6YqRwuqQP1rnb6885aM/1775725362554.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRcnXVy4TnB14TdXpjUQPE9edVBKpWzJHy3LbAe37axxu/1775725362658.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV54hBgxwvcx47btHCbo5W3aV5jK99ZEfdCrrE4T8XPEf/1775725362895.jpg) The damage that occurred was really quite severe, not only was the land carried away by the landslide but wood and stones were also carried away, until now the damage that occurred can still be seen clearly, how this disaster has damaged and eliminated much of the beauty. The result is that during the day the roads will be covered in very thick dust and this will really disturb the surrounding air, but when it rains the roads will become slippery and muddy due to the mud. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVJ1c2fLHZbo7ZebHYiNCqgwAqtyCKfyDpsXRFjy4EJxt/1775725362955.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcHpBXGkLzpfkqLZxqD9TFwGQ9W2eJYL75Gnr9iRFsynJ/1775725363036.jpg) However, the natural scenery still looks quite beautiful, especially if we see it from the top of the hills, how the blue tawar sea water adorns our eyes and the mountains towering behind it. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaTcR8Zbw1XEkeHWstFxB6kFb3Rkb1HBrMKy6Qg9qzwf2/1775725363101.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ3LRAPPPzn18KqLnSmyrZVFWrK7V5uFzsBXYGVZq5zba/1775725363162.jpg) And now it's time for us to explore several open natural tourist destinations in the Ujung Pasir tourist village, one of the most famous natural tourist destinations in this village is Jiva. Jiva is a popular camping ground-based tourist destination in Takengon City, located in Bintang Village, Lut Tawar District. It's actually been around for quite some time, but this was my first time visiting,i didn't know how amazing it was, but from what I'd seen and heard on social media, it was truly extraordinary. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR9jZRUKFRPh38Wp9THEm1rr1tDProGGdXQi1Me62Qhmd/1775725363232.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbSiVmE9eU75sjvrmHCFNFAQTAriDyMa51YdNFvcT7Csa/1775725363303.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeL2P81cTy6HpLAjb9JhQ7LDUtBwqSs2TDJD5WC4G11HW/1775725363383.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTA6bnFHBoL62EXvM3c89fHidMc6s7sZmAp6MLV3Kicns/1775725363475.jpg) To get to this tourist spot, we have to pass through the village road again for about 1 minute, it turns out that this tourist destination is on the edge of the tawar sea and the view can be seen from the road. As soon as I saw the natural scenery offered by this tourist spot, I immediately added this place to the list of the most beautiful tourist destinations in the city of Takengon in my opinion, it's a shame I always missed this place before,everything this place has to offer looks absolutely stunning, from the natural scenery, the facilities available to the many tents standing on the shore of the tawar sea. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUbtUUA4vx2mB5bNMxyHhZpHQsPtyaxDTv6cKJbNwJAjC/1775725363546.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXwKVUYyqjZ3T2qah8We91XmEcFfjSbWGgB9TNibAaDcf/1775725363616.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSeSMGEqnTRbzC6Zfo8j3P2cupLEjHTYH9yNW9PCJAddK/1775725363681.jpg) From the main area, we can see that there are lots of chairs and huts in this place, and also lots of tents lined up neatly on the edge of the tawar sea. This place has succeeded in making me comfortable and now it's time for me to explore it. ----

Life is a responsibility Be yourself, keep learning and don't hesitate to start😉

If you like other travel posts, you can see them on [Worldmappin Community](https://v3.ecency.com/created/hive-163772) and you can also participate there. If you are curious about the places I have visited so far, you can see them on [my personal worldmappin map](https://worldmappin.com/@riyat) And you can also find me on [Ecency Discord](https://discord.com/invite/m9MyMSWx)

----

Thank you very much for reading my post till the end, I am here to say thank you very much 🙏

All images are mine, I took the photos using the Infinix 10 pro cellphone and I edited the images using the Lightroom application. I'm @riyat. See you again in my next post ♥️

Hello everyone! It was a really long journey in my Bantayan Island travel, and until now the enthusiasm lingers. From my ship voyage to Bantayan Island to visiting Blue House by the Cliff, we have now come to my next destination that amazed me unexpectedly with the beauty of Bantayan. This island really carries hidden gems waiting to be explored, and this one I have visited is known as Baigad Lagoon, a lagoon and a beach nestled in Sta. Fe, Bantayan. This lagoon was magnificent and stunning; I have never seen one like this, and probably it has set my standards of stunning lagoons. It was then that I knew this island is really deserving of what we call rich in tourism because it truly is, and I’ll let you experience this island through this blog. ![Messenger_creation_FB291473-2F4E-4F9E-A5BF-3FAC88861071.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23wqkWjbSkMiBg9vDxcruhrvNXHiDmQmT6HPE9oREUWBWSVRMbuZzXoxskuqxBRu3YJoV.jpeg) ![9e350f43-8519-4587-9963-c84a859a25c2media_editing.tmp.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23xyVEAzYHownh3MjHm8zUkx2fxoGSzVDipTQiBTGmTcwurbcr33GnhZ1iBRBWEiaXa88.jpeg) ![6a9b2cef-646d-4501-906f-a5a7e08dd289media_editing.tmp.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23wWw3CT4R1UUJH6Yhm6chBuGovaDU8qAWBi9MZzEH4MEEivFEHWkAAiMv2z2tL3B5Kmb.jpeg) ![Messenger_creation_15996568-3BBF-4AB8-BBF5-E7BC5595E196.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23wqi9RmmgQLnrHW7qXHBcbBrY4M8PriF1wuiAVDj5Cc5u1JE9Lq97te8xuQT6vs9UjDE.jpeg) ![Messenger_creation_2C57F439-DA98-48C0-8026-029E9F0335A7.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23zknCt8e8KhBhhFLif8kRuyXSYpr19zctD8BgotANFE1xZJ5nQMAkwMrBc6ALBx1bykQ.jpeg) ![Messenger_creation_DA41019F-00B9-4527-8884-E39E80D6818A.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23y8swNPG1uxhQHRwDLTmV7Ky68DPfa5GfJ7XshGYv2k3NJT14r34KeuBbicMyem2u9zz.jpeg) ![13657a5a-58ad-4467-a383-5f984a7a967cmedia_editing.tmp.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23xp2BiHs4ssUcYzQWeKTiJLZ9L7j1t2mRHrdsogsNG8CWBJNKJWhQWx7objxktYTFSdP.jpeg) ![ffde2844-ddc6-40fd-8964-115c007ed1famedia_editing.tmp.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/Eou9BMjQkm8GvLDANGCdP1adD9dY15dneYJLUjXLA5ahaguRSRL3yCgM7XopiERttpy.jpeg) Baigad Lagoon was an entrance-free, accessible lagoon in Baigad, Daanbantayan, right on the eastern coastline of the island. It was then before that this place was not commercialized, but time came when the owner of the lagoon decided to commercialize it and enhance its quality through tourism. When we used Maps to navigate the island and search for the lagoon, we stumbled upon a road where coconut trees are alive, and it was where the Maps said the lagoon is hidden. When we were on our way, an old man stopped us and asked what intent we carried to enter such a place. When he heard the word lagoon, he then redirected us to another road where the lagoon can be accessed. ![Messenger_creation_152840EC-10FC-47A5-AC88-A4B4BC92639A.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23xosQHN13xNdJxCMBccHc653WrPGvMnyLcjtSvo2J9dPNZRy4gVsuynFBZcuPLDQuU8t.jpeg) ![0530316a-9847-429e-b0b3-7b465d7f1e58media_editing.tmp.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23vhz28bT67CK1R5mdFZBoxQ9FoWk8fejfX7R9ftqZJfCyEfrkyPYKt7iZeStry24LZML.jpeg) ![d6fe96c4-14e4-4c79-9196-9af7ba876ba6media_editing.tmp.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23yHkxox16HLytwPMpE7ez9FNwDmjJWbhD28uTp5N6kgbr9D4xYywQ5a9vAx3zbmXGMg5.jpeg) ![Messenger_creation_E23733EB-FD44-4D91-A368-2A0EE0EE0C8C.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23xyQgXVKdM7zxosjdMwz5SvooUnr1yrmA5Cg1tKHnWXEe3JnejzCpAgpbj4FJuxLFX4L.jpeg) ![b1d743d4-4f54-4cb9-996f-fc7f80f040edmedia_editing.tmp.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23wqZdFgtWwHhs4XgUQpXFpToEm3tMPfeoyMTDwA2S7MQV4EHNNrz8uzUbe4j1E269oGM.jpeg) As we entered the fence where a small hut is installed, we then learned the lagoon is still in the same spot, but we needed to take a pumpboat to access it since the only way to reach it is through the shore, which is impossible because the tide is always high in this part; hence, a pumpboat is needed. is exclusive only for tourists who have room accommodation. Pumpboats are also floating on the water, on standby for tourists or visitors who want to go home. Many tables with umbrellas are installed and are free for use. We picked the right one that overlooks the lagoon, which I will be sharing with you in the next blog for this destination since there is still so much to talk about this lagoon. ![Messenger_creation_5A5C214B-AA76-481B-82E1-939236660F95.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/EpA1z57t3c4XxY7QnfnPkPtPf1PYWzWBWqe4oYaUEJaLFQWMddgtPmqqvQYHKbZG1Up.jpeg) ![Messenger_creation_3CCAEFC9-0F6C-466B-A556-477DA25A6290.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23wX1eesUGGZggi5mCwCNdv2hARHjD5eSMnfLxiH4orEZP4o7iUZe2aPtiCvxy2h52JPj.jpeg) Sometimes, we would approach the lifeguard for a life vest since we were already warned about the lagoon’s current that can push us farther to the other end of the water. We borrowed life vests for safety and swam around the said area where it is safe to swim, and when the current diminishes, we can pass through the water and walk around the other side of Baigad. ![Messenger_creation_35501477-9F4E-46CF-8C35-DC2FCC287C44.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23wWyULp6bmK2krPaWR9WyUWEomtkcb8V9CaT4UNAfN5QCXj2RXQn6dZX4npcPWGjTjm3.jpeg) ![Messenger_creation_4606C82E-8BC6-4011-8A0E-86C9EFEC41B0.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23wgPvTTBHRL9jBCnuEZLdmfexMoYQib6n8Zam5VhqyL86t3jZ4CKYre2opYuPyEKxxNF.jpeg) ![Messenger_creation_B556C3EA-A855-4E29-B453-77B0E1B870E0.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/241tZL2zPgf18Tz99L8xCUYmig9z5Mu8nquG2LesaDy1oE9T1xUXjfJPgqxF2kL1a8mf3.jpeg) We took photos at this arc-like signage since it really gives me memorable vibes. Things like this that mark a destination are really of interest to me. I took a photo of my boyfriend making fun of himself, and we were laughing while enjoying the view. There were corners in Baigad that are full of hammocks for tourists to rest after swimming. We rested here for some time and even slept before leaving the lagoon. It was breezy, refreshing, and the sea is a perfect view and escape from life’s responsibilities. ![Messenger_creation_E66086BB-334E-4A6C-9330-43232392117B.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/23xp47bDvN11EyQSRxWo8BAgUkg5wGxx6KcvfZoL3H2wFFeUsJmAwyc6TQdFwA643pzTz.jpeg) ![Messenger_creation_12F9037F-A337-49EE-BB64-B8730426602C.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/whosee/EokdaVanoVbLMrJGKyyzAPKzMpBzv4T1ovZdMV9ovvzpaHC7fJG3yVMNdFw5fqoAjLu.jpeg) The sea in Baigad Lagoon faces another island known as Virgin Island, which is home to a fine stretch of beaches and is really small in geography. This one is at least 30 minutes in travel from Bantayan and has gained popularity ever since 2015 when Virgin Beach was opened. The sea is clean, clear, and home to diverse aquamarine mammals and species. As I sat there, feeling the breeze and watching the calm waves touch the shore, I realized that Baigad Lagoon is more than just a destination—it is an experience that lingers even after you leave. The quiet moments, the laughter, and the beauty of the place all come together, making it one of those hidden gems that truly define what Bantayan Island is all about.
**You Can Follow My Bantayan Journey Here:** [Bantayan Island: The Island That Redefined My Idea of A Perfect Beach](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@whosee/bantayan-island-the-island-that-redefined-my-idea-of-a-perfect-beach) [The Ruins: An Abandoned Cliffside House That Became the Heart of Bantayan Island// Bantayan Travel Part II]( https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@whosee/the-ruins-an-abandoned-cliffside-house-that-became-the-heart-of-bantayan-island-bantayan-travel-part-ii) [Not on the Map but Worth the Risk: Discovering a Cliffside Blue House and Turquoise Paradise in Bantayan]( https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@whosee/not-on-the-map-but-worth-the-risk-discovering-a-cliffside-bluehouse-and-turquoisie-paradise-in-bantayan) [//]:# (!worldmappin 11.182444 lat 123.787422 long A hidden turn led us somewhere unexpected—what secret lies beyond this road, and why is everyone talking about it? d3scr)

![image_20260409_181719_0000](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23uFZnVJk6g6vAd5QeyA6V3VkEkn3fSpnq5sBEyY7qwKWXtzGcukv6tZvyWJE5jHkB2rx.png)



Finally, we got to visit Ubot Falls in Villa Aurora. It was such a nice trip and honestly the place is so beautiful. As soon as we arrived we were surrounded by so many trees and plants. It really feels like you are deep inside nature.
 

![image_20260409_181720_0002](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23vsLEHrLHAKywfjWt8j6jj5hD5CBMKEhwyFUJDzBdbuJUWtxZzTe3ZGbNnyLgjWXqt8Z.png)

The falls itself? It was amazing. The water flows down from the rocks and it looks so clean and fresh. The view is really pretty way better than just seeing photos. It feels so peaceful there just listening to the sound of the water.
 

![image_20260409_181720_0001](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/244A4viRQHLi6nvBhpiFfHpLEN33H3hUcCtAgjxfS99Z4kKoTCehwF4j9cNKreATY3ga4.png)

What really surprised us was that they have rooms there! We did not expect that at all. Usually when you go to falls you just bring tents or sleep outside. But here, they have actual rooms you can rent to sleep in.
 
![image_20260409_181720_0004](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23vsNB7XRE3bhDd7MhsEVjjKqVN6HMFyVDQrH2ncELKS2R1Tmw2bsqP9CSWfJRUaPjyEQ.png)


That was such a big help for us. After walking around and enjoying the place we did not have to worry about setting up anything. We just went to our room, and it was ready. It’s simple but really okay and clean.
 
![imagr_20260409_181722_0010](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/243frmJZf6Z9o1ti3YFj7xv4nA3QTXZ2oA62ahffFhP2WG2fYmvePkhroHn6hrU9BDuYb.png)

Being able to stay overnight made the trip so much better. You get to enjoy the falls during the day and then you also get to experience it at night. It gets really quiet and cool, perfect for relaxing.
 
![image_20260409_181722_0011](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23zbS3ZsXZQPBs7sbqhMUDZNaedX4oUVvNZgdbRdzrWpomcGAnZuCb4MvWovdmKbxbUT3.png)


Waking up in the morning there was awesome too. The air is so fresh and you can see the greenery right outside. It feels so good to start the day like that far away from the city noise.
 
![image_20260409_181722_0012](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23x19B4u1KvrUK1YCFq6VfNNMGnsXY9rHqS7iJR8aH3qJvxom1DPNiEFfjnRG4PuyTGn9.png)


We spent a lot of time just swimming and chilling in the water. The pool at the bottom is nice, not too deep so everyone can enjoy. The water is really cold and refreshing especially when it’s hot outside.
 

![image_20260409_181720_0003](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23vi8P1xt1Hkcp36jhyekfBtJsXKFmvm9DoToAaEXUPoFV7FhMHtbqtq6sRocfqCXMpD5.png)

It washes away all your tiredness right away. We just stayed there, splashing around and having fun with friends. It was just pure enjoyment and good vibes the whole time.
 


![image_20260409_181721_0007](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23w2qMfk8C19zm1WmUMg8rMXvA67FFBcfHfLHMUR3uSYWho5DcUv8AUvmk26s7wsjtPHb.png)

They also have nice paths and railings so it’s safe to walk around. Even if it gets a bit slippery you can still walk easily. You can go around and see different views of the falls.
 


![image_20260409_181721_0006](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23tmFr6PMQbmcjLF45dScfBNF5PLt2j4qRodY3o3ADHabHDpt6WhGKxELA9wLPwUScYtG.png)

Everything looks well taken care of so you can just relax and not worry about anything. The place is really nice and clean which makes the experience even better.
 
![image_20260409_181721_0005](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23wC7vmkJPx2X9FnoNi1Q9g2daK5tsnUSuS4oDxjR7v9FxVrBedjfWtx3m3cWWLkLS3Wg.png)

Having rooms available is really a great idea. It makes everything easier especially if you are with a big group or family. You have your own space to put your things and sleep comfortably.
 

![image_20260409_181721_0009](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23vsNg7nosXk5mtxtmU6JdQoNa37ECAVBkSr1rsyMC2fpjH4Zcxh7dcoHtu8cyhSFA7GE.png)

No need to rush going home because you can just stay there and take your time. You can really unwind and enjoy the beauty of nature without any hassle.
 

![image_20260409_181721_0008](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/olang23/23zRyL6mTFtN4efM2tEc7u2h3RXWtVjqn33J7UrbpRsmy97ULKkFoUD7WUrrPpLwr9fGk.png)

We really loved our visit to Ubot Falls. The beautiful scenery plus having a comfortable place to stay? It’s just perfect. We had so much fun and we definitely want to go back again!

Hello everyone! What a beautiful day to talk about awesome places right? I'm super excited to share with you all about this really pretty resort I saw. This place is located in Brgy. Ibona in Dingalan, Aurora. And seriously it's really, really beautiful!
 

![image_20260409_100556_0001](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23zv4zvKLRXnsd3KtP1rvpc2zDVFPY7wVpPmtAKqchseoEjJLALjRoJdBUU7HyBuPsfRy.png)

It's one of those spots that just
makes you happy the moment you see it. It has so much to offer for anyone who wants to just chill out and have a great time. It's truly a place that puts a smile on your face right away.
 

![image_20260409_100557_0004](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/245HeZshPean12UdmYmZS6vAtTkaD8DYVkgmMkCJQbrp3XQHWE9GunQd6xUPA7NJwFUcC.png)

When you first step into this resort the first thing that really catches your eye are these super cute little houses I mean A-frame cotages. They are lined up so neatly like tiny little dollhouses.
 

![image_20260409_100557_0003](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/2432BDi3r247RDvMLgBG7TdJNeFhwgZC6QKU5wthCEZJKMBjAkhLxYA7Qj92MgVpxNH7n.png)

They all look cozy and inviting. Each one has a lovely reddish brown color with a bright white roof which just pops against the green grass and the blue sky. They look like the perfect little spots for a vacation.
![image_20260409_100557_0005](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23s9Lwvz7PuBiJuZSxQi7fSANANHgMmDqFULe5BrqUKVXuUrS6G4yaLLwAkdSJNeTcJPD.png)

These cottages give off a very homey and unique vibe not like boring hotels. Outside each cottage there's always a little space with a picnic table and benches. This is perfect for just hanging out.

![image_20260409_100557_0006](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23xyV9Ly4xBQBXovHie5WuxLAgJ6UiorrooodFpTukyp4UhNkuNDXu8Ew8h1rHmJAcWoC.png)


Maybe you can have your morning coffee there or enjoy some snacks. You can sit there and feel the air listen to the sounds of nature and just watch the world go by. It’s such a simple but thoughtful touch.
 


![image_20260409_100557_0002](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/242DESqDrq9wFK21he3swnRdXgjooMVtYEWM5vpQe3YXu6npCoPHV5ca7EPPo86mb7tHV.png)


This makes your stay even more comfy and gives you your own little private spot right outside your door. The whole resort grounds are really well maintained. The pathways are either made of smooth concrete or nice little stones.
 


![image_20260409_100558_0011](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/242DC8KgnDWsKWiyvR2DSrpSxU7acnemVvRK2j46MNtZsbUodrGjbaqwnSUgWfKu6H4ms.png)


This makes it super easy and pleasant to walk around. And the grass? Oh it's so green and perfectly trimmed like a huge carpet spread out everywhere. You can tell that the people who run this resort really work hard.
 
![image_20260409_100558_0007](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/241ZfWWN1cBwYm3HQL1E4r8Sm7hV4oSRkYZAHCjF8pMbcA5ZUadrWqfRyozAUYbTpcNSW.png)


They put in a lot of effort to keep everything neat and tidy. It makes the whole place feel clean, welcoming, and very relaxing to stroll through. And then there are the palm trees! So many of them, tall and graceful.
 
![image_20260409_100558_0010](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23yJANnbfHFFGZxdDT14T2WC9TsDxwwjnDu5HY7CKzwETrpj74hAM37JQYGpCAutqMV8o.png)

They sway gently in the breeze. They provide natural shade from the sun and just add so much to that tropical island feel. When the sun hits them they look even more majestic. They really complete the picture of a perfect beach resort.
 

![image_20260409_100558_0009](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23zRvo4YDw2mbk1Rmv42m3aGfi4oYJe4DEtxeLR8PgHB3LMEAzQTBqWHrWUfAjHKypTf9.png)


They make you feel like you are truly on a vacation far away from all the busy city stuff. As you walk deeper into the resort following the pathways you eventually reach the ocean. And wow 😲 what a sight!
 


![image_20260409_100558_0008](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/243WMewtagkh7brR89ufJZQng4VtF7oBWqnrtGQW7DCrajLSWZYYzFPmiu856E2ZQVXGC.png)


The path leads directly to the beach and you can see the waves crashing beautifully against the shore. The water looks so clear and inviting with different shades of blue and green. The sound of the waves is just music to your ears.
 

![image_20260409_100559_0015](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23xedbheNxZpq9wTeaBaZZY2BTRhUyo5bNyWmbaeCEkzZjbgWUY9u5NTiwfMSVasWoqcu.png)


It makes you feel calm and peaceful. It's truly a breathtaking view that reminds you of nature's beauty. Near the beach there are also some lovely outdoor areas that look like dining or chill out spots. They have these charming thatched roofs.


![image_20260409_100559_004](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23wWrf7CtiYjBgzxmw2aHQSfETVVVxKgV759HHC8XfNgxGYyt3wMP263HoEiVpGAStBt8.png)



These roofs give off a really authentic, laid back island vibe. You can just imagine sitting there enjoying a delicious meal or sipping on a refreshing drink all while feeling the gentle sea breeze and listening to the ocean. These spots are perfect for gathering with family or friends.
 

![image_20260408_174356_0000_](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23zkg8UoD712uoqQzZcWSiosmW4B5Nss1G72G9daYkAijghH2YsQze6perJPN1e5wDK8S.png)

But wait there's more! This resort also has a beautiful swimming pool and it's placed right by the sea! How cool is that? You get the best of both worlds you can take a refreshing dip in the clear blue pool or go for a swim in the ocean.
 

![image_20260409_100558_0012](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/243LxnXTkKBHJyDy2KUT6zgiiVpXrwVbSADrQsWK6yGhVxZWe6Av6NPVLP15fraQ73Hrz.png)

Whatever you feel like! The pool area looks super clean and modern with nice lounge chairs around it. It’s perfect for sunbathing relaxing and just soaking up the good vibes. The overall feeling of the resort is just incredibly relaxing.
 

![image_20260409_100600_0016](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/245HaYzj6mQJFfGsc8DfCYEgJKcquNgfmtydLoQ4GuqThLvgZFCsNNrcUt4E6PfvQscZi.png)

It feels like a little paradise hidden away in Dingalan, Aurora. Everything is designed to make you feel comfy and peaceful. From the cozy cottages to the well kept grounds and the stunning views every detail makes for a great stay.
 

![image_20260409_100601_0017](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/levieshome/23xeduAF3p118HzNNwirPqVzLQxCWWq4QpRuEt3pH5jxCHaSZrb2d8LC4fUjmLxngCvLU.png)

So, if you are ever planning a trip and looking for a truly beautiful and relaxing spot you should definitely check out this resort in Dingalan. It's a hidden gem that combines cozy places to stay amazing beach access a cool pool and a super chill feeling. It's the perfect place to make good memories!

# A Backdoor into the Arches

I don't know any of you visited some of the popular National parks in 2025-26, due to budget cuts, a lot of the facilities are currently restricted. Many parks, including Arches National Park had "timed entry" in 2025. Thankfully in 2026 it is taken away again, so just like before you can enter the Park at any time in 2026. I was there with my family over the Easter weekend for a short trip. Arches National Park can feel overwhelming at first—crowded entrances, long lines of cars, and packed parking lots. For our recent trip, we decided to do things differently. Instead of joining the line at the main entrance, we rented a Jeep Wrangler Rubicon 4WD and entered the park through the Willow Springs Trail, a lesser‑known backcountry route. It ended up being one of the highlights of the entire trip—especially for our kids.


![IMG_5246.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EqqusuD6fjqjKcCnCwkTxWLRjZihFoWKpFJnNsrqsA1obDi1wW1uNJ8zuj1Qvz4gWp4.jpeg)


# Willow Springs Trail

One thing worth mentioning upfront is that finding the entrance to Willow Springs Trail is not straightforward anymore. The old, direct access from Highway 191 (to BLM road 378) —which many older maps and blog posts still reference—is now blocked. You can’t simply turn off the highway and drive straight onto Willow Springs Road like you used to.


![IMG_5154.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Eq7KXRc5KyivnM1q6T88SrB2QUoo63bQbWowFKYxKZ2qHX3jW19ZVBjPNoT8k4AdQ3y.jpeg)




Today, the only practical way to access Willow Springs Trail is through the newly created Utahraptor State Park entrance. This initially caused some confusion for us, because it feels like you’re entering a state park just to get to the trail.

![IMG_5149.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EpJWFx4xLa73fKBM5JWAnr6dioLqZPYnRHTaCspVTYfPy7QTFwuzbudKgdS8av5FuN4.jpeg)

The good news—and this is important—is that you do not need to pay the Utahraptor State Park fee if you are only transiting through to access Willow Springs Trail. There’s no separate booth for Willow Springs itself, and as long as you’re just driving through to reach the Arches backcountry route, there’s no additional charge. That was a relief to confirm before heading in.

Navigation-wise, signage can still feel a bit sparse, so having an offline map or GPS track helps. Once you’re on the correct dirt road, though, it’s obvious—you’re heading straight into wide‑open desert with sandstone fins rising on both sides.

# Trail Details

Willow Springs Trail is not technical off‑roading, but it’s real 4WD driving. Sandy washes, slickrock sections, mild ledges, and washboard surfaces kept things interesting, and the Rubicon handled it effortlessly. For the kids, every bump and dip was a thrill. They called it “desert roller‑coaster mode,” and every sandy section came with laughter and excited commentary from the back seat.



![IMG_5147.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Ep5kMCBJtnXJoR78WUy2kB2Yuav3HirHmAZctNN1PXvHepJMA5aPtr7aem2Jk6UkzQu.jpeg)

One of the best parts of this route is how quiet it feels. With the windows down, we could hear the wind, the crunch of tires on gravel, and the occasional shout of excitement when the Jeep climbed over rock ledges. We stopped briefly to explore the dinosaur track area along the road—a bonus that added a paleontological layer to the adventure.


![IMG_5135.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Eq355Dsm5otAwYetVH8k8FMztK8NZmN1JB7w3yqCM3iYAVqJk1puKnrp3zjTxnNBXUW.jpeg)

There are Dinosaurs footprints to look at along the way. I have been able to show the kids both Theropod and Sauropod prints.


![IMG_5140.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/23tbwM7DQGN41qLuBsjG8y6imzmhoZVp7Phhwi8WGiGiyQVfTLqkBu6R9rvyqMSkp3Pkm.jpeg)


![IMG_5137.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EoGxrqkLYAQFLF8VbdyZfQjZJBMp5KwszfS4bQbJTBeiGf8vkjzaNw3UvhBFd6ennaZ.jpeg)


After roughly eight miles, the dirt road suddenly met pavement. Just like that, we popped out near the Balanced Rock parking area, officially inside Arches National Park—without waiting in a single line.

# Devils Garden and Landscape Arch

From Balanced Rock, we joined the main park road and drove straight to Devils Garden, knowing it gets busy later in the day. Getting there earlier felt like a small victory after our quiet backcountry entry.

We parked, pulled out our packed lunch, and claimed a shaded picnic table. Eating lunch surrounded by towering sandstone fins and spires is one of those small moments that sticks with you—and it gave the kids a well‑timed energy reset before hiking.

The hike to Landscape Arch is ideal for families. The trail is well maintained, mostly flat, and full of interesting rock formations that kept the kids engaged. They ran ahead, stopped to inspect rocks, and asked a steady stream of questions about how arches form—questions we answered with varying degrees of geological confidence:) Kidding! My wife did her PhD here in the Arches and Canyonlands, and we have many field seasons together here. Kids are often overwhelmed with our constant chatter, in a good way!


![IMG_5186.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Eq7KycyM53BqAkPVeGhf6qz94vDVuw1ySM3zKTDLyFCRfmwRwgv9YtbTYCmrHERrzRh.jpeg)



Standing beneath Landscape Arch is humbling. The span is unbelievably long and thin, and seeing it in person makes you appreciate just how delicate it really is. We lingered, took photos, and enjoyed one of those rare quiet moments where even the kids paused to stare.


![IMG_5180.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/Ep7tCPSeTQXeby3Qyx6HPnggaHet5u69pcjM8nn5yQz9c9HDoDhoHFyuCETd9DfET8J.jpeg)



# Sunset at Delicate Arch (not quite, but close)

After Devils Garden, we spent the afternoon driving through the heart of the park, stopping at viewpoints before heading toward Delicate Arch later in the day. Timing this hike closer to sunset was intentional—and absolutely worth it.

![IMG_5224.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EogMtF6bsoKBLhpfbggDanc9A5GrLQMngvqtP64cbQWRxV7vHXqGRBvZ8JuvfUeME29.jpeg)

The Delicate Arch trail is more demanding, especially with kids. There’s steady elevation gain, exposed slickrock, and very little shade. But the trail is visually engaging the entire way, and the anticipation keeps everyone moving.



![IMG_5234.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EpA26qyAAtM7TJa5AwXbJNT8kbRzMNGrHESdKabSEYf99Rxi2uXiyjYNMHuiAeTPGiC.jpeg)

There are couple of smaller arches nearby along the trail which kids enjoyed at lot more, as they were free of crowds and they could do whatever they wanted over there.

![IMG_5253.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/azircon/EopqUGMh61WWfhBEr9xgZxtS889mAop3wmDvZRE7uHnVyuQYRp13pqZ3vMtpgzbsZYH.jpeg)




As the sun dropped lower, the colors of the rock deepened—reds shifting to orange, shadows stretching across the bowls and fins. When we finally rounded the last corner and Delicate Arch came into view, the kids nearly forgot how tired they were. We didn't stay up all the way to sunset, which is 7:40pm, because then we would have to get down in the dark. I didn't want to do that with kids, so we left around 6 pm and got down in about 45 min to our car.






# Why This Day Worked So Well

Entering Arches via Willow Springs Trail set the tone for the entire visit. It wasn’t just about skipping the lines—it was about turning the drive itself into an adventure. The off‑road experience engaged the kids from the start and made them feel like part of the journey, not just passengers heading to the next stop.

Combining that with iconic hikes—Landscape Arch for awe and ease, Delicate Arch for challenge and drama—made it feel like a perfectly balanced day: adventure, hiking, family time, and unforgettable scenery.

If you’re visiting Arches with kids and want a more memorable, hands‑on experience than the standard park entry, renting a 4WD and using Willow Springs Trail is absolutely worth considering. For us, it turned a crowded national park into a personal adventure—and gave the kids a day that they will remember.
